newsitem.title: UK: Internet forex dealing service launched in London.
newsitem.headline: Internet forex dealing service launched in London.

text.p: Currency-trading company Currency Management Corporation on Monday launched a 24-hour live online foreign exchange dealing service on the Internet.

Clients download a software package from the Internet, receive currency price quotes from CMC's dealers and a real-time news service from news supplier CNN and can then place their order via the screen, the London-based company said.
Customers can buy or sell 27 currencies, trading in major pairs such as dollar/mark and dollar/yen, as well as crosses such as mark/yen and sterling/mark.
Managing director Peter Cruddas said the company was targeting players such as corporates, investment managers, private individuals and small- and medium-sized banks.

"There are many tiers to the forex market. We're not looking at the five-star elite top tier because that's already been taken care of with electronic broking and the money-broker market," Cruddas told Reuters.
The minimum dealing size is for $100,000 or its equivalent, but there is no maximum trade. CMC makes its money from the spreads quoted by its dealers, which include its commission.

The trading service was launched unofficially last week and 1,500 people downloaded the software -- the "MarketMaker" package by Information Internet -- in five days, Cruddas said. There were 200 to 300 dummy trades per day.

"I'm looking to pick up 1,000 clients in the next six months," he said. CMC dealers currently quote only spot and forward rates, but Cruddas said the service would eventually expand to offer futures and options too.
